name: Kat3x Action Doctor
author: office4llm

sections.description:
Manual read-only diagnosis for the current single site. There is no time limit,
license key, paid feature, resend, repair or background scan.
Action Scheduler: current status and scheduled UTC time in a bounded window.
WP-Cron: stored events and the DISABLE_WP_CRON configuration flag.
WooCommerce webhooks: current status and stored failure count; history is incomplete.
Email channel: none supported in 0.1. No real email adapter is installed or enabled.
No multisite operation or cross-site parameter is supported; network activation is refused.
A source that cannot be read is non-observable, distinct from an available empty source.
Observed late means older than the observation time minus 300 seconds. It does not prove
a stopped worker, failed hosting, disabled system cron or any definite cause.
At most 50 records per source and a positive window of at most seven days are accepted.
Webhook status is current, not a reconstruction of past transitions. Logs may be absent,
rotated or retained for a shorter period; the plugin does not infer missing deliveries.
Each source has its own UTC read time. A dossier is not an atomic snapshot across sources.
The reader returns only enumerated states, counts, UTC times, response-local aliases and
observation limits. It does not return action arguments, hook names, URLs, payloads,
recipients or raw error text.
The reads are also registered with the WordPress Abilities API, for a user with
manage_woocommerce. An assistant you connect to the site receives the same reduced,
signed result.
The plugin makes no HTTP request, opens no socket, sends no email, registers no
scheduled callback and runs no delivery test.
The signature covers declared observations and integrity; it proves no delivery or cause.
The interface text is in English. The release ZIP contains no translation files, only the
POT template; translations can come through translate.wordpress.org. Machine result
codes do not change with locale. Read the complete bundled guide in docs/en.md,
docs/it.md, docs/de.md, docs/fr.md or docs/es.md; technical details are in docs/reference.md.

Privacy

Observations are reduced locally before signing. No personal field is hashed for export.
No report or diagnostic log is persisted. A user may choose to save the response.
Protect local node key options, backups and site copies. Other site components are outside
the observation window and this plugin’s claim. External persistent object-cache backends
have not been certified by this release; shared node reads use WordPress option APIs.
sections.installation:
1. Use the release ZIP on a site with WordPress 6.9 or later, PHP 8.1 or later and WooCommerce.
  2. Activate on one site. Activation provisions local node identity and signing material.
    Signing needs the PHP sodium extension. Without it the plugin still activates, stores
    no identity, and each read returns the fixed message “Local node unavailable”.
  3. As a user with manage_woocommerce, open WooCommerce > Action Doctor and read the dossier.
  4. Keep the returned receipt locally or pass it to your own assistant if you choose.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin resend a failed action, webhook or email?

No. It only reads the supported local sources. Email channel: none supported in 0.1.

Does an accepted mailer event prove receipt by a recipient?

No. The release has no real email adapter and does not establish recipient delivery.

Does read-only cover installation and activation?

Diagnostic requests do not write SQL, files or reports. Activation, identity provisioning,
key maintenance and uninstall are separate lifecycle operations which do write options.
The private signing key is stored locally in a database option with autoload disabled.
Database access or code execution can read it. Protect backups and site copies; assign
staging copies their own identity. Uninstall removes local options, not external revocation.

Which permissions and parameters are needed?

manage_woocommerce in the current site is required before any source read. The UI also
checks a nonce. Abilities accept only da_utc, a_utc (UTC timestamps), and limite (1..50).
No site ID, SQL, path, callback or free-form filter is accepted. Node must already exist.

Does the plugin have paid features?

No. Every function described here is in this plugin, with no time limit and no license key.

Why does an empty result differ from non-observable?

An empty result means the supported source was read within the selected bounds and
returned no accepted records. Non-observable means the source is unsupported or
could not be read. Neither result proves that every past action was delivered.

Can I diagnose another site in a network?

No. Only the current single site is supported. Site and blog parameters are refused.

Where are the instructions and troubleshooting steps?

Open docs/en.md inside the release ZIP, or docs/it.md, docs/de.md, docs/fr.md or
docs/es.md. Each guide covers the local page, result limits, fixed error messages,
privacy and signature verification. The technical reference is docs/reference.md.

Does a delayed event identify the cause?

No. The comparison uses the read time minus 300 seconds. It does not identify a
stopped worker, a hosting fault or a failed recipient delivery. Inspect the source
and your existing operational evidence before choosing any repair outside this plugin.
sections.changelog:
0.1.2

Admin page: the form nonce is read by its key, sanitized and verified before any other input; no other form field reaches the plugin logic.

0.1.1

Every PHP file stops when loaded directly. The page reads the request method through
WordPress sanitizing functions and the two table reads use prepared table names.
The readme states the interface language and the translation path. No behaviour change.

0.1.0

First bounded read-only diagnostic release, five guides and explicit limits.
